division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the north division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's farms_and_country_seats clause. The places held before the plat stay where they were held: Beaubien's on the lakefront reservation, Clybourn's on the North Branch, Robinson and Caldwell's on the west ground. They are not seated by any of this — they are the reason the policy has to say 'outside the plat' at all. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

ruled.what_happened: DRAWN UNDER A RULING, NOT A QUOTA. The household model drew this house married at 3, and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell; no woman the town already holds fits him either. T-2021 ruled that such a house is given its whole drawn family while the town stays inside the model's own range for 1 July 1835 — at most 3,265, the November count — and this house was admitted under it. The wife and children are the ones the model drew for this house from its own seeds, at the `reconstructed` tier; no source names them, and none says N Murphy married.

kin.note: N. MURPHY AND MRS. M. FRAUNER ARE HUSBAND AND WIFE, AND THE REGISTER MARRIED THEM. Entry 1 of Father St Cyr's marriage register, at Chicago, 1834: 'N. Murphy' and 'Mrs. M. Frauner', celebrated by J. M. I. Saint Cyr, filed as st_cyr_marriage_001_1 and st_cyr_marriage_001_2 in data/research/church/records/st_cyr_marriages_1834_1839.json. THE DATE IS AT OR BEFORE THE SCENE: they were married on the day this dataset reconstructs. THE GRADE IS WHAT A PARISH REGISTER IS WORTH FOR THE ACT IT RECORDS. The St Cyr register is the contemporary record OF this marriage — the date, the place, the celebrant and both parties by name, written by the priest who performed it — so the relationship is read off a record rather than reasoned to. The rung these two people carry (G2c, inferred) is a ruling about RESIDENCE: a parish register naming somebody is weak evidence that they LIVED in the town and strong evidence that the act happened, and this row claims only the second. THE LIMIT: the reading is transcription_mediated — the Illinois Catholic Historical Review's printed transcription, not the manuscript — and a transcription can mangle a name. It cannot invent a couple. NO IDENTIFICATION IS BEING MADE HERE. Both cards were minted FROM this entry and carry its record id in church_evidence, so the two people this row links are the two people the entry names; nothing is matched by surname. A KINSHIP IS NOT A PLACEMENT: neither household's position, arrival, trade or membership rests on this row.

associated_with.note: THE REGISTER NAMES HIM AT A PARISH ACT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CLAIM. Father St. Cyr's register carries this person as groom in st_cyr_marriage_001_1, dated 1834 and tied to this card by the church crosswalk's rule G2c. `st_marys_church` is his church, which the structure record states — 'St. Cyr selected the lot in 1833 and ... was succeeded by Father O'Meara only after 1837, so he is the pastor across the whole scene window'. THIS IS NOT A MEMBERSHIP ROW: being a witness, a party or a decedent at a Catholic act is what the register states, and the dates are the act's own, which is why `from` and `to` are the same day and the row is not carried forward to the scene date.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('murphy_n:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.
